feature1.prompt: Strip unused annotations from count queries: Optimize the query processing logic so that any annotations not referenced by filters, other annotations, or ordering are removed from the generated SQL query. For instance, a count() query should produce the same result as when no non‐essential annotations are added, thereby improving performance in complex queries. The implementation should ensure that count queries execute without the unnecessary overhead posed by unused annotations.
feature1.hint_texts: Feature 1 involves modifications in the query processing logic. Developers need to update the core routines that build and execute count queries so that any annotation not actually used in filters, ordering, or further annotations is pruned. The changes primarily affect how annotations are collected and processed, with attention to functions like get_aggregation and solve_lookup_type. Focus on modifying the behavior in django/db/models/sql/query.py and django/db/models/query_utils.py to minimize subquery wrapping by removing unused annotations.
feature1.entrypoint: Files to modify: django/db/models/sql/query.py (in methods such as get_aggregation and solve_lookup_type) and django/db/models/query_utils.py (in the refs_expression function and related annotation lookup logic). These changes will form the core optimization for count queries, ensuring that only necessary annotations make it into the final SQL.

feature2.prompt: Enhance query processing by integrating reference tracking: Update the query evaluation mechanism to support intelligent detection of which query expressions are actually referenced. This enhancement will allow the system to determine which annotations are truly necessary during count queries, ensuring that only those referenced by filters, other annotations, or ordering are retained. The goal is to achieve an optimization similar to how select_related calls are omitted in count queries, thereby improving performance.
feature2.hint_texts: Feature 2 focuses on introducing a reference-tracking capability within the query processing framework. Developers should add a new method, get_refs, in both django/db/models/expressions.py and django/db/models/sql/where.py that collects and aggregates references from source expressions or child nodes. The method needs to correctly compute the set of dependent annotations so that other components can decide whether an annotation is required. Ensure the new functionality integrates seamlessly with the existing optimization logic.
feature2.entrypoint: Files to modify: django/db/models/expressions.py (add the get_refs method) and django/db/models/sql/where.py (implement the get_refs method). The changes should ensure that get_refs returns the accurate set of references for query expressions and that these results are utilized by the query processing routines.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the core query processing framework, including files such as django/db/models/sql/query.py, django/db/models/query_utils.py, django/db/models/expressions.py, and django/db/models/sql/where.py, as well as the data structures handling annotations and query expressions.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature 1 (annotation pruning) relies on accurate reference information provided by the new get_refs methods introduced in Feature 2. A clear interface and contract for get_refs must be agreed upon so that the returned reference sets are correctly used to mask or keep annotations. Joint integration tests should verify that count queries are optimized without losing necessary annotation data.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature 1 and Feature 2 need to collaborate closely on how annotations are tracked and pruned. It is important to discuss the design of the get_refs method and agree on how its output integrates with query transformation logic. Regular coordination will be required to address potential conflicts in the annotation data flow and to ensure the overall query performance improvements are achieved.
